subject.title: [Feature]: Intelligent Model Fallback with Wildcard/Auto Selection

question: Should OpenClaw add provider-family wildcard/auto fallback, grouped `fallbackFamilies`, catalog-derived fallback candidates, or keep only explicit flat `fallbacks`?
rationale: All viable designs add or change public model fallback/config behavior, and repository policy treats fallback/config/provider routing as compatibility-sensitive product direction.

options.title: Design one explicit fallback contract
options.body: Pick a single additive contract, align schema/docs/runtime availability gates, and require upgrade/fresh-config proof before implementation.

options.title: Limit scope to catalog-derived fallbacks
options.body: Use the narrower https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/60922 direction only if maintainers want configured model catalogs to drive fallback but not wildcard provider-family auto selection.

options.title: Keep explicit flat fallbacks only
options.body: Close this direction if maintainers prefer operators to list exact fallback models and rely on docs/doctor guidance for provider model drift.

recommendation.title: Design one explicit fallback contract
recommendation.body: Pick a single additive contract, align schema/docs/runtime availability gates, and require upgrade/fresh-config proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant schema, fallback, and docs history points most strongly to Peter for the product/config contract decision.
